ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (273) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, italics, footnote markers, and deletion markup preserved.
Translated fresh from the Russian; where a passage coincides with the calendar or a finished story, the reviewed R003 English was reused and changed only where this text differs.

These are Tolstoy's manuscript drafts of *What For?*; No. 1, the first complete draft, is titled «Непоправимо» (Nepopravimo, 'Irreparable') and calls the family Przyzdecki and the elder sister Ernestyna, and the translation follows the finished story's names and phrasing wherever the wording coincides, keeps Tolstoy's deletions struck through and the editors' angle brackets (< >) as printed, and renders «палки» (palki) as 'sticks,' «розги» (rozgi) as 'rods,' and «шпицрутены» (shpitsruteny) as 'spitzrutens.' Forms found only in the drafts are kept as printed: «Панни» (Panni, the Polish word for an unmarried woman, used of the mother), the landlady's Russian «Иосиф Станиславович» (Iosif Stanislavovich), the Cossack «Степан» (Stepan), «Руфим Пиотровский» (Rufim Piotrovsky, the historical Rufin Piotrowski) as 'Rufim Piotrowski,' and «Приорский» (Priorsky) as 'Priorski,' while the one-letter variant «Сероцинский» (Serotsinsky) is normalized to Sierociński. Part B follows the finished *What For?* for names and recurring phrases (Rosołowski, Sierociński, Szakalski, Ludwika, Wanda, "the police chief" for «полицмейстер/полициймейстер» (politsmeyster/politsiymeyster), "the little lady" for «барынька» (barynka), "sentenced to be driven through 1000"); spelling variants of one name are normalized as there (Ludwika for «Людвига/Лудвига» (Lyudviga/Ludviga); Józek for «Иусек/Иузек» (Iusek/Iuzek)), while two forms Tolstoy uses only in the drafts are kept distinct: «Жозя» (Zhozya, a French-style pet name for Józef) as "Zhozya," and «Шокальский» (Shokalsky) in a deleted passage as "Szokalski" beside the usual Szakalski. The Cossack's «ваше высокоблагородие» (vashe vysokoblagorodie, the address due to a staff officer) is "Your High Honor"; Albina's Polish «разем, вшистко разем» (razem, vshistko razem) is given in Polish spelling as "razem, wszystko razem" with Tolstoy's own parenthetical glosses translated, and the footnote label «Дальнейшее написано по зачеркнутому» (dal'neyshee napisano po zacherknutomu) is rendered "What follows is written over the deleted text."

Source observation: [4] The mother is called «Панни Пшиздецкая» (Panni Pshizdetskaya); Polish panni/panna is the word for an unmarried woman, and the finished story has «пани» (pani, 'Mrs.'). Possibly a slip for «Пани». Kept as 'Panni'.
Source observation: [9] The dictation «La maison написали? du prisonnier [^11]... opens with « but has no closing »; the English closes the quotation after the ellipsis.
Source observation: [18] «чтобы-нибудь» (chtoby-nibud', not a word) is a slip for «что-нибудь» (chto-nibud', 'something'); translated 'something'.
Source observation: [32] An empty «<sup></sup>» tag follows the [^19] marker (apparently a conversion artifact); kept as printed.

Source observation: [63] The last sentence breaks off grammatically: «между бесконечными непаханными поросшими прошлогодним серебристо белым ковылем, дороге» ('between endless, unplowed, overgrown with last year's silvery-white feather grass, road'). The noun after the adjectives (perhaps 'steppes') is missing, and «дороге» ('road') is repeated. Translated as printed.
Source observation: [83] Stray comma in «Альбина, продолжала» ('Albina, went on'); omitted in the English.
Source observation: [84] The heading prints «ІІ» with Cyrillic/Ukrainian І letters instead of the Roman numeral II; rendered 'II'.
Source observation: [92] Stray comma in «и, после, всех попыток» ('and, after, all the attempts'); translated 'and, after all the attempts'.
Source observation: [96] The heading reads «(рук. 11, к гл. V)» without «№» (No.), unlike the other headings; kept as 'MS. 11'.
Source observation: [98] Stray comma in «как сама с собою, называла его она» ('as she herself, to herself, called him'); the English comma happens to fall in the same place.
Source observation: [105] Stray comma in «бывшим ксендзом и, приором Сироцинским» ('the former priest and, prior Sierociński'); omitted in the English.
Source observation: [113] The priest's name is spelled «Сероцинского» (Serotsinskogo) here and «Сироцинский» (Sirotsinsky) elsewhere; normalized to 'Sierociński'.

Source observation: [114] «слабым прерывающимся стоном голосом» ('in a weak, breaking groan voice') is garbled, perhaps for «стонами» (stonami, 'by groans'); translated 'in a weak voice broken by groans'. The Latin prayer ends with a closing » but has no opening «; the English supplies the opening mark. «secundam» is kept as printed (Vulgate: secundum).

Source observation: [120] «Приорский» (Priorsky) is not otherwise known. It is perhaps a slip for «Пиотровский» (Piotrovsky), the one successful escaper named in the deleted passages of blocks 33, 34, and 36. Kept as 'Priorski'.
Source observation: [126] Six men are sentenced to 7000 blows here, but [128] in the same draft says «тех пятерых» (tekh pyaterykh, 'those five'); Tolstoy's own inconsistency, translated as printed.
Source observation: [129] «содатам» (sodatam) is a slip for «солдатам» (soldatam, 'to the soldiers'); translated 'to the soldiers'.
Source observation: [130] The heading reads «рук. 12» (ruk. 12) without «№» (No.), unlike the other headings; translated as printed 'MS. 12'.
Source observation: [156] «воскрикнул» (voskriknul) is a slip for «вскрикнул» (vskriknul, 'cried out'); translated 'cried out'.

Source observation: [218] «ее отчаяние перед потерей всякой надежды спасения и страха за своего мужа было еще сильнее» (genitive «страха» (strakha, 'of fear') and singular «было» (bylo, 'was')) differs from the parallel [204] «и страх … были» (i strakh … byli, 'and fear … were'); possibly a slip, translated as printed ('and of fear for her husband was stronger still').
Source observation: [228] «взглянул на ее» (vzglyanul na ee) is a slip for «на нее» (na nee, 'at her'); translated 'glanced at her'.
Source observation: [232] The heading «(рук. № 9 <sub>f</sub> к гл. XII)» has a stray «<sub>f</sub>» where a comma is expected (transcription artifact); kept as printed.
Source observation: [272] [^27] «вытянутыйбатальон» (vytyanutyybatal'on) lacks a space ('a battalion drawn up'); translated as two words.
